qualifying_findings.title: Open WebUI 0.11.0 vulnerability records receive in-window NVD updates across RAG, OAuth, tools, knowledge, terminal, and chat boundaries
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: NVD updated an Open WebUI 0.11.0 security wave inside the run window. The updated records include DNS-rebinding and IPv6-transition SSRF through URL/RAG/image/OAuth fetch paths, sub-resource validation gaps in the Playwright web loader, OAuth token-exchange audience binding failure, cross-user knowledge attachment reads, knowledge-base cleanup object-ownership gaps, terminal preview origin script execution, terminal WebSocket approval-boundary loss, tool-source disclosure to non-admins, KaTeX stored XSS, regex denial of service in knowledge search, automation recurrence event-loop exhaustion, chat task cancellation before authorization, image-generation permission bypass, and standard-channel message authorship failures.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD in-window update wave plus CVEAWG records, GitHub security advisories, patch commits, and Open WebUI v0.11.0 release references
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Open WebUI versions before 0.11.0 across web loader, URL/RAG ingestion, OAuth, chat, channels, knowledge, terminal, tools, markdown rendering, and automation scheduler paths; fixed in 0.11.0 according to records.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Self-hosted AI chat and RAG systems combine browser fetches, retrieval indexes, user content, OAuth, terminal access, and server-side tools. This cluster shows how weak per-boundary validation can turn ordinary AI platform features into SSRF, credential exposure, cross-user data access, session takeover, permission bypass, and service-wide denial of service.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Owns broad Open WebUI product/entity context if a general product page is needed.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: May own general self-hosted assistant operation practice; do not duplicate broad workflow guidance here.

qualifying_findings.confidence_notes: High confidence that NVD records were updated inside the window and identify concrete security fixes. Ingest should distinguish NVD update timing from original August disclosure timing.
follow_up_actions: Deduplicate into one or more durable Open WebUI security leaves instead of one page per low-level route unless independent maintenance needs require splits.
During ingest, inspect GitHub advisories and v0.11.0 release notes for exact patched-version and remediation language.

qualifying_findings.title: Flowise 3.1.3 vulnerability records receive in-window NVD updates for agent, memory, tool, CSV, MCP, and SSRF paths
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: NVD updated Flowise vulnerabilities inside the run window. The records cover RCE and code injection in agent memory/record-manager DataSource options, custom tool baseURL source interpolation, CSVAgent/Pyodide and prompt-injection execution paths, read_pickle deserialization, chatflow/agentflow deletion authorization confusion, IPv4-mapped IPv6 SSRF in HTTP/MCP/document-loader paths, and a Custom MCP server npx auto-install bypass using npm_config_yes.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD in-window update wave plus CVEAWG records, Flowise GitHub security advisories, patch pull requests, commits, and Flowise 3.1.3 release references
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Flowise versions before 3.1.3 across chatflows, agentflows, CSVAgent, memory nodes, record-manager nodes, custom tools, HTTP security, document loaders, API chains, and MCP tool launch paths; fixed in 3.1.3 according to records.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Flowise is an LLM flow and agent builder where user-configurable nodes can become execution, fetch, memory, and tool-launch boundaries. This wave shows that AI builder features need strict separation between untrusted prompt/data inputs, code templates, dependency installation, internal network fetches, and workspace authorization.

qualifying_findings.title: Agno PythonTools and ShellTools prompt-injection RCE receives in-window NVD update
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: NVD's in-window update for CVE-2026-37003 describes Agno up to and including 2.5.8 as vulnerable to unauthenticated remote code execution through prompt injection. PythonTools and ShellTools pass unsanitized LLM-generated arguments to exec(), runpy.run_path(), and subprocess.run(), allowing malicious instructions embedded in processed web pages or documents to trigger arbitrary code or OS command execution on the host server.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD in-window update plus CVEAWG record and researcher detail reference
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Agno up to and including 2.5.8; PythonTools and ShellTools; LLM-generated arguments to Python and shell execution sinks.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The finding is a direct prompt-to-execution boundary failure in an agent framework. It shows why execution tools must enforce typed arguments, approval gates, sandboxing, and untrusted-content separation even when the model selects tool parameters.

upstream_routing.security_wiki: Owns the prompt-injection-to-RCE and agent execution sink control implications.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: May own general agent-framework selection and execution-tool workflow guidance.

qualifying_findings.title: llmware 0.4.6 collection filters allow SQL injection and cross-document disclosure
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: CVE-2026-85689 was visibly updated by CVEAWG and NVD inside the run window. llmware 0.4.6 interpolates filter and lookup values directly into SQL WHERE clauses in SQLite and PostgreSQL collection database paths. The key allow-list does not sanitize values, so attacker-controlled filters reaching Library.block_lookup and Query text-query helpers can bypass intended collection/document scoping and, on PostgreSQL, enable boolean- and UNION-based SQL injection.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: CVEAWG in-window update, NVD in-window update, public GitHub issue, source-file reference, and VulnCheck advisory
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: llmware 0.4.6; llmware/resources.py; Library.block_lookup; Query.text_query_with_custom_filter; Query.text_query_by_author_or_speaker; SQLite and PostgreSQL backends.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Retrieval libraries often enforce document, collection, tenant, or user boundaries through metadata filters. SQL injection in those filters can disclose rows outside the intended retrieval scope and contaminate or exfiltrate private context supplied to LLM workflows.

upstream_routing.ai_wiki: Owns broad llmware framework/entity coverage if needed.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: May own general RAG library selection and metadata-filter governance practice.

qualifying_findings.title: PraisonAI web_crawl SSRF patch-bypass records receive in-window NVD updates
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: NVD updated CVE-2026-55523 and CVE-2026-55524 inside the run window. PraisonAI versions before 1.6.58 and 1.5.128 through 1.6.57 perform SSRF checks only on initially supplied URLs in the web_crawl tool. The fetch path follows redirects or re-resolves hostnames without revalidating the final destination, allowing attacker-influenced agent/tool URLs to reach loopback, private-network, or cloud metadata endpoints and return the body in tool results. One record frames the issue as an incomplete fix and patch bypass for earlier web_crawl SSRF advisories.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: NVD in-window update plus CVEAWG records and PraisonAI GitHub security advisories
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: PraisonAI before 1.6.58 and 1.5.128 through 1.6.57; praisonaiagents.tools.web_crawl_tools.web_crawl(); httpx and urllib redirect/fetch paths; fixed in 1.6.58 according to records.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: Agent web-crawl tools are often exposed to model-selected URLs and untrusted web content. A validate-here/fetch-there gap lets agent browsing cross network trust boundaries and leak internal service or metadata responses back into the model/tool result stream.

upstream_routing.security_wiki: Owns web-crawl SSRF, patch-bypass, and agent browsing network-boundary implications.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: May own general agent web-crawl workflow design and operational practice.

qualifying_findings.title: ASCII smuggling technique from prompt injection is reported in active phishing-filter evasion campaigns
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: In-window secondary reports summarize Microsoft Security Research's September 3 primary post on a high-volume phishing campaign using invisible Unicode tag characters. The technique, previously popularized for AI prompt injection and XPIA, was used to split finance-themed lure words so recipients saw normal text while raw-text keyword detectors saw obfuscated tokens. The reports cite Microsoft telemetry showing a February spike from roughly 21,000 daily signature hits to more than 1.3 million, a later peak above 2.3 million, and about 150 finance-themed sender domains accounting for most detected volume. Microsoft recommends stripping or normalizing Unicode tag characters and other invisible code points before filtering and before AI ingestion.
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: Official Microsoft primary research outside the exact window plus in-window reputable secondary coverage
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Email filtering and AI-assistant ingestion pipelines that process raw text containing Unicode Tags block characters U+E0000 to U+E007F or other invisible code points.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: The same invisible-text mechanism that can hide instructions from users while exposing them to models is now being repurposed for phishing evasion. Defenders should normalize text before both traditional detection and AI-assistant summarization so hidden characters do not become an evasion or XPIA channel.

upstream_routing.security_wiki: Owns the prompt-injection/XPIA evasion mechanism and AI ingestion normalization control.
upstream_routing.ai_wiki: No broad AI entity update needed except Microsoft provider context if relevant upstream.
upstream_routing.ai_dev_wiki: May own general agent content-ingestion and tool-output normalization practice.
